title: The Stone Watchers - A History of Rapa Nui and the Moai
author: Ethan James Farrell
description: A custom popular history from Ethan's collection: The Stone Watchers: A History of Rapa Nui and the Moai, subtitled At the Edge of the World: How a Tiny Island Built Giants, Lost Everything, and Kept Its Secrets. Beginning with the island as 'the navel of the world', it covers Polynesian voyaging and first settlement, the moai as deified ancestors, the Rano Raraku quarry, theories and experiments on how the statues 'walked' to their platforms, the later Birdman (Tangata Manu) cult at Orongo, and the undeciphered rongorongo script. A central chapter re-examines the popular 'ecocide' collapse story in the light of newer archaeology. It then follows European contact, the catastrophe of Peruvian slave raids and disease that brought near-extinction, Chilean annexation and the sheep-ranch era, and the modern Rapa Nui revival. It sits in the library as context on sacred landscape and ancestor cults rather than as an esoteric text.
editionNote: Curator-supplied PDF and EPUB from the organised ebook collection. One format was converted from the other (PDF from EPUB).
